findings.issue: The new Section 9 MODE PACKAGE INDEXES table states 71 deep-research scenarios and 69 deep-review scenarios. The package playbooks state 72 and 70, and the folders hold 72 and 70 scenario files. The scope added this table and copied the stale package-README counts, so the hub index now contradicts the package indexes it links to. Case: a reader planning release coverage from the hub playbook budgets for 71 and 69 scenarios where the packages require 72 and 70.

hasScope accepts any non-empty array, while scopeEntries drops non-string and blank entries. A proposal with scope ["   "], [123] or [null] therefore passes the relevance check at line 403. On a review run the review-target containment check then runs over an empty scope list and passes vacuously, so a node scoped nowhere is admitted, counted toward the frontier, and can never be answered by a finding. The other required fields (question, evidence) are rejected when blank; scope is not. Case: a leaf emits "scope": ["  "] and the node is admitted instead of pruned relevance.

evidence.cmd: node -e 'const {checkProposal}=require("./.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs"); const caps={maxDepth:3,maxChildrenPerNode:6,maxRootChildren:8,maxFrontierNodes:10}; const reviewConfig={reviewTargetType:"files",reviewTarget:"src/app.ts"}; for (const scope of [["   "],[123],[null],["src/app.ts"]]) { const r=checkProposal({question:"q",evidence:"e",scope,parentId:"root"},new Map(),caps,[],{reviewConfig}); console.log(JSON.stringify(scope),"->",r===null?"ADMITTED":"pruned:"+r); }'

fix.new: return Array.isArray(scope) && scope.some((entry) => typeof entry === 'string' && entry.trim() !== '');

findings.issue: The expansiveBudget comment says the ceiling 'binds for a four-dimension review from two seeds on', but the function returns 24 at one seed: 2 x 4 x (1 + 3 - 1) = 24. The test at frontier-admit-review.vitest.ts:571 asserts 24 for one seed while its name repeats the same claim. B-08 reports the docs sentence and the test name; this is the code comment that seeded the wording, and it is the only place the claim sits next to the formula.

fix.old: // review from two seeds on. Twice the node count keeps the half-budget node cap
fix.new: // review from one seed on. Twice the node count keeps the half-budget node cap

findings.issue: The prose says 'A node needs one iteration per dimension in its universe, the four canonical dimensions plus any custom name', but configuredReviewDimensionCount in frontier-admit.cjs counts only the configured reviewDimensions list. For reviewDimensions ["correctness","performance"] the code uses D=2 and derives 12 iterations, while the reducer's universe is five dimensions and the prose implies 24. The test at frontier-admit-review.vitest.ts:565 asserts 10 for ["correctness"] with three seeds, confirming the code's configured-count behavior. The same sentence is in .skilled/commands/deep/review.md:100. Case: a custom-dimension review is sized for two dimensions while the doc tells the operator to fund five.

fix.old: A node needs one iteration per dimension in its universe, the four canonical dimensions plus any custom name.
fix.new: A node needs one iteration per configured dimension, the four canonical dimensions by default plus any custom name.
